items.prompt:
When a text flags what is not yet known, it marks:
A) uncertainty
B) a summary
C) a title

'Strong' textual evidence is the:
A) most convincing evidence
B) longest paragraph
C) first word

An inference is a conclusion drawn from:
A) evidence and reasoning
B) a guess
C) the title

Read.

The study found a link but notes the sample was small and calls for more research.

What does the text leave UNCERTAIN?
A) whether the link truly holds
B) who wrote it
C) its page count
items.answer: A) whether the link truly holds

steps: Small sample = uncertain. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) whether the link truly holds

items.prompt:
Read.

After the local law passed, crime fell, but national crime also fell.

This leaves uncertain:
A) whether the law caused the local drop
B) that crime fell
C) the date of the law
items.answer: A) whether the law caused the local drop

steps: Confounding national trend. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) whether the law caused the local drop

items.prompt:
Why do credible texts sometimes flag UNCERTAINTY?
A) it makes the text more credible and precise
B) it hides the facts
C) it is never useful
items.answer: A) it makes the text more credible and precise

steps: Honest about limits. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) it makes the text more credible and precise

items.prompt:
Read.

A report claims a supplement 'may' boost memory, citing one study of 12 people with mixed results.

The strongest reading is that the claim is:
A) well established
B) uncertain and weakly supported
C) proven false

steps: Tiny sample, mixed results. Key is B.

items.prompt:
Which is the WEAKEST evidence that a program reduced poverty?
A) incomes rose in the area
B) the program's logo was blue
C) fewer families needed food aid
items.answer: B) the program's logo was blue

solution.answer: B) the program's logo was blue
